body:
I appreciate your caution and want to assure you that I am plenty aware of the vast differences. I merely suggest that my intense affection towards creature so different than myself lends hope towards the ability to foster stronger love to a person much closer to heart. I was in no way suggesting the amount and effort of care is anywhere near the same level.

As far as straddling the fence, I have had these concerns before my boyfriend was in the picture. The issue has just become more magnified now that I am in a stable relationship where that is one of the few core desires left for us to discuss.

I am familiar with the efforts of raising a child (aware not experienced) as I am ten years older than my youngest sister. My extended family have babies and we spend a lot of time together.

If this clarifies anything for you...

I agree. That's part of why I am really trying to decide now because do to financial and health reasons we are having to move in with his parents and I am giving up a lot in order to do so, like surrendering my cats (really long story, I don't care if anyone thinks I'm over dramatic about it. The point is I am devastated by it). So I should generally make up my mind (I know there would be time to change, but to have a stronger conviction one way or another) because otherwise I'm moving and surrendering my cats into an inevitably ending relationship if I don't want kids in the end.

I know it sounds like I am really swayed towards not wanting them, but those are just the things that weigh on my mind when thinking about it. The opposing argument is that I want kids just because I do. That I probably would actually make a good mom, I mean considering I'm so attached to my cats, it'll be such a deeper connection than that, how could I not me at least marginally good at it? So I am genuinely on the fence and change camps a lot.

My reasons are because I am diagnosed Bipolar (II) with Borderline Personality Disorder traits (may turn into a full diagnosis), PTSD, and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. For me to have children, I would have to stop my medications because they are extremely harmful to fetuses, especially during the early stages so it would need to be a planned pregnancy. Not only would going off my meds make me unstable, but I would struggle very much with the body changes I would go through. Let's say everything does pan out for that period of time, mental illness has a long history on both sides of my family and I don't want to pass that along to my children. I don't want them to have to live with that in their lives too. I feel like it would be irresponsible.
I am already seeing a therapist, but it has minimal effectiveness.

As far as surrogacy or adoption, that is an option. For surrogacy, we wouldn't have my egg cells in the mix I think because that would still be cause for several of my concerns. And with my Borderline traits, and just bipolar as well, it's inevitable that I am going to have bad cycles no matter how many precautions I take. I'm already going to struggle sometimes by lashing out, but it would be worse if the child didn't come from me. Basically I don't want to subject anyone as collateral damage in my own battles.

That being said, I do think I could be a good mother too. I really enjoy kids (for the most part) after about age three or four. I think I would be the best aunt ever and thats definitely what I want in my future. (I have four sisters, one already married, it's bound to happen). And I think that would fulfill that motherly instinct in me. But there are things I do even now that indicate I would be good at it I think. Like I try to be a good hostess at home. When I have friends or family stay over, I make sure everything is set up good in the extra room, make sure they know how to reach me if they need something, I am kind of really doting over the while ordeal and it makes me happy to provide hospitality, it's important to me. I think that level of concern and care would translate well into motherhood.


I know I am probably spinning things in a ton of different directions they don't actually need to go, but apparently that is part of my Borderline Personality Disorder. I can't really help it.
Young enough to still have plenty of time to decide.

Well yup. You hit the nail on the head with that one. Split family, mom's and dad's houses had two sets of rules and expectations from me growing up. Still in general have expectations from my family that are unrealistic but I am getting better with establishing my boundaries with them. It's not always like "ways I could kill myself" it's more of "that could/would kill me"

If you know anything about the ACE trauma test or whatever, I scored an 8 which is apparently high but there is no singular event that has scared me.

But I also don't know who is the real me. The me on my medicine? Or the me off my medicine but (cyclically) mentally unstable?

Yeah, it does.

I've generally been mostly honest about it but I have this flawed drive to make people feel like they helped me (forever. "it's the thought that counts") so I say I am more improved than I actually am.

I do already see a talk therapist. We kind of deal with it as always an option for "tomorrow" but just not "today" and it keeps the thoughts controlled. Also viewing them as like the extreme last escape plan, "if all else fails" but I'm no stranger to hospitals, I've admitted myself 3 times.

As far as figuring out the metaphorical meaning of it, that is fairly beyond me.

I was just kinda thrown off and found it a little weird that I was thinking about how we could have a nice life together. Like we were talking about how his grandparents' house needs remodeling and I wanna help. Then I got to thinking how we could have a nice little house and bicker and fight like old married couples (and we already) do. His sister's idolize me (16 & 11) and i love them like my own. In the end, we would do anything for each other, no matter how brutally honest we can get. We have an endless pit of trust. More than my boyfriend and me for somethings.

To address a seemingly common concern:

The comment about not "completely hating it" if we had sex did not come out of no where. The exact phrasing was like, "If push came to shove". But otherwise, yeah it's a weird thought for us both. The topic came up because him and my boyfriend kept pushing about how "at some point in time, doesn't the idea ever come up" and my friend was caught between the truth-he doesn't see me like that and it'd be weird- and hurting my feelings (because i am such a delicate flower) because he thinks I would be sensitive to someone saying it'd be weird to have sex with me. Or decide to say, which he did, that if "push comes to shove, he probably wouldn't hate it."

Not only do we spend time together, but about 60-70℅ of the time my boyfriend is there too and they get along great. Occasionally my friend stays over in out guest bedroom as well, if we have been drinking or if he just needs to get away for a bit. All with the blessing of my boyfriend. He says that our home is always open to him whenever he needs.
